{{Quote|And it was his so-called Unification Policies that have drawn so many worlds back into the web of Republic influence.|Paak, a member of a separatist group, on Tarsus Valorum|<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two" />}}
The '''Unification Policies''' were a set of legal guidelines and recommendations proposed by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]] around [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] as part of the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] to unify the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] after the devastating [[New Sith Wars]]. The main opposition for the policies came from many separatist groups that wanted to keep their [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] out of the Republic.

==Description==
In [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the end of the [[New Sith Wars]] with the [[Ruusan campaign]]&mdash;the last set of battles of the wars&mdash;left [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] weakened. [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]] proposed the Unification Policies to help reunite the [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] that had started to show the seeds of rebellion after the war;<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia" /> he wanted to bring those [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] back into the web of Republic influence.<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two" /> Valorum proposed the Unification Policies as part of his [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]], a series of proposed reforms that were meant to restructure the whole Republic. After the policies were enacted, the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] was able to enforce the regulations of membership in the Republic.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia" />

[[File:Tarsus_Valorum-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[Tarsus Valorum/Legends|Tarsus Valorum]], the man who proposed the Unification Policies]]

==History==
The Unification Policies were first proposed following the New Sith Wars, which ended with the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|final battle]] of [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] in 1000 BBY. Because several separatist groups, such as the [[Anti-Republic Liberation Front]], saw the Unification Policies as a form of bullying, nearly one hundred small rebellions arose following the policies' approval.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia" /> [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], the last remaining [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], worked behind the scenes to pit rebellious organizations against the Republic, hoping to distract the Republic from the secret survival of the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith Order]]. One such event happened in [[990 BBY]] on the planet [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]], where Bane's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]], worked to get a small Anti-Republic Liberation Front cell to perform a kidnapping of Valorum, by then the former Supreme Chancellor. One member of the cell, a [[Gender/Legends|man]] by the name of [[Paak]], was originally against the idea, but his hatred of the Unification Policies was so great he eventually went along with the plan to kidnap Valorum. The members of the cell attempted to [[Kidnap attempt on Serenno|kidnap]] the former Chancellor but were stopped by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Johun Othone]].<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two" /> Over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], several separatist cells tried to oppose the government's ability to keep [[Star/Legends|star]] systems in the Republic, but their efforts were in vain. The Republic stood for almost another [[19 BBY/Legends|thousand years]], and many of the rebellious groups eventually disappeared.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Unification Policies were first mentioned in ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'', published on [[December 26]], [[2007]]. They were later described in more detail in the [[2008]] compendium ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.
